newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla, mulls streamlined bond counsel pool.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla, mulls streamlined bond counsel pool.

text.p: Florida's Dade County finance committee has proposed creating a new, streamlined bond counsel pool to replace the unwieldy group of 16 firms the county currently uses.

Commissioner Jimmy Morales, who chairs the finance committee, said at a Thursday meeting that the pool was so large the county used different firms for each issue, leading to inconsistencies in its documents and creating more work for county staff.
"The system seems to be broke. The number has to be reduced," Morales said.
"We have got to repair it," agreed assistant county attorney Gerald Heffernan.
Morales proposed choosing one firm as disclosure counsel for all of county bond issues and selecting a pool of three or four two-firm teams to handle the rest of the work.

The committee asked City Manager Armando Vidal to draw up a new request for qualifications, which would be issued if the full commission approves the plan later this month. Current pool members will be allowed to re-bid.
The county chose the current pool just a year ago, after a long and emotionally charged debate over whether to reward the big, experienced firms or nurture small, local and minority-owned firms.
The county compromised, asking the firms to create joint ventures that paired each major firm with a small or minority-owned partner, then selected eight two-firm teams.
Under the new proposal, the county would keep the joint venture structure, but choose no more than four two-firm teams.

The committee also proposed that its three financial advisers be asked to submit reports twice yearly outlining any changes in the firm's ownership and detailing any lawsuits, regulatory action or investigations involving the firm. The county already reqires its underwriters to submit those reports before each bond issue.

The finance committee also gave preliminary approval to sell depreciation rights on its Metrorail cars via a lease-back agreement with the Bank of New York. The proposal, which still must be approved by the full commission at two hearings, would give the county a one-time payment of $7 million.
